body: This seems to be related to debug builds.  `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo` and `Release` both work
oh interesting, I think I hit this as well trying to debug build for an unrelated change but did not realize it was due to my change.
IIRC the backtrace was extremely deep, pointing to a stack overflow; I had looked into it briefly but couldn't figure out which line was debug-gated. Now that I know it's my fault, I'll try harder.
Yeah, I also had a massive backtrace.  Let me know if I can help debug

Looks like this is happening while setting up the docstring for a defaulted argument of type torch::onnx::OperatorExportTypes (which is an affected enum) in python_ir.cpp.  repr() and int() are mutually calling each other. Looking into why.

The `__repr__` of an enum straightforwardly calls int_ on it, no debug-gating shenanigans (pybind11.h:2642)
int_ in this case is hitting the "try next overload" error, which calls repr() (pybind11.h:1182), so there's the infinite recursion. not yet sure why this doesn't affect release builds.
Note to self: we should have kept debug build clean and revert PRs that regress it, but it's in a pretty bad state now

also not sure why int_ is hitting the "try next overload" error. has to be that we messed up type casting.

probably should just revert this and debug offline.

added `py::native_enum`, and also had to add overhead for that new way
to bind enums on the critical path for calling functions that take
regular old `py::enum_`s as arguments (for example, `__eq__`).
